title: Flood emergencies, pension changes and tourist flat VAT
summary:
Flood emergencies bring urgent warnings in Valencia and the Balearic Islands. We cover pension changes, the voting-rights appeal affecting Spaniards abroad, and VAT on tourist flats awaiting parliamentary confirmation, alongside election and workplace news.

Enjoying Spain Daily? Support us: https://buymeacoffee.com/spanified

segments.speaker: Inna
segments.body: Classes are suspended today on Mallorca, Eivissa and Formentera because of flood risk. Valencia has activated emergency situation two.

segments.speaker: Dima
segments.body: There are urgent instructions for people in the affected areas. We'll start with those.

segments.speaker: Inna
segments.body: Good morning. It's Monday, the nineteenth of October, and this is Spain Daily, from Spanified dot com!

segments.speaker: Dima
segments.body: I'm Dima, here with Inna. Today, pension changes and VAT on tourist flats. First, the flood emergencies in Valencia and the Balearic Islands.

segments.speaker: Inna
segments.body: El País reports flooding in La Safor and Marina Alta, coastal districts in the Valencia region. The regional government activated emergency situation two today and called in the military emergency unit. Aemet's rain warning is red for southern, inland and eastern Mallorca. The rest of Mallorca, Eivissa and Formentera are under orange warnings.

segments.speaker: Dima
segments.body: Classes are suspended today on Mallorca, Eivissa and Formentera. The Balearic government has also requested military emergency help. Valencia's emergency alert covers places including Dénia, Xàbia and Gandia. The Girona river has burst its banks in Els Poblets, flooding areas near the river channel.

segments.speaker: Inna
segments.body: For people in the affected Valencian areas, the alert says not to cross flood-prone places. Stay away from rivers, ravines, seafront promenades and the coast. Move to high ground.

segments.speaker: Dima
segments.body: The instructions specifically say not to enter basements or garages, and not to use lifts. Inna, what are people in the Balearics being asked to do?

segments.speaker: Inna
segments.body: Avoid travel and outdoor activities. Stay away from torrents, flood-prone areas and basements. The Balearic alert also tells people at home to go to upper floors.

segments.speaker: Dima
segments.body: Please check the official alerts and Aemet's warnings for your area. The Valencian coast faces life-threatening flood risk, and dangerous conditions are disrupting schools and travel in the Balearics.

segments.speaker: Inna
segments.body: On pensions, the government plans to approve next year's increase after inflation data becomes available from November twenty-seventh. Economy Minister and First Vice-President Carlos Cuerpo says existing law guarantees the rise, according to 20 Minutos. He believes a caretaker government could approve the decree before this year's end.

segments.speaker: Dima
segments.body: Wait, a caretaker government can approve a decree like that?

segments.speaker: Inna
segments.body: That's what Cuerpo believes, yes. He says the rise is secured by a law already passed, so it doesn't depend on a future government. I see

segments.speaker: Dima
segments.body: Staying with pensions, Heraldo reports retirement changes from January first next year. Retiring at sixty-five with a full pension will require at least thirty-eight years and six months of contributions. Otherwise, the standard retirement age is sixty-seven. Voluntary early retirement remains available, with pension reductions.

segments.speaker: Inna
segments.body: That's a long contribution history. mhm For someone approaching retirement, the question is how much they've paid in, not just their next birthday.

segments.speaker: Dima
segments.body: Exactly. Leaving earlier can mean a smaller pension. Reaching the contribution threshold matters when weighing that choice.

segments.speaker: Inna
segments.body: El País reports that a Social Security benefits decree is planned for cabinet approval tomorrow, October twentieth. It would improve support for several groups, including gender violence victims on sick leave. They would receive sixty percent of base salary initially, rising to seventy-five percent later in the leave period.

segments.speaker: Dima
segments.body: When would that higher payment begin? For someone unable to work, the timing of the income change matters.

segments.speaker: Inna
segments.body: After the twentieth day of leave. Parliament's standing committee would need to confirm the decree within a month. The government needs support from the left and the Basque Nationalist Party.

segments.speaker: Dima
segments.body: The Constitutional Court begins considering today whether to accept the ombudsman's voting-rights appeal, El País reports. It concerns more than a hundred and sixty thousand Spaniards abroad, naturalised under the descendants' citizenship law. The Supreme Court's interim voting suspension remains in force ahead of the November twenty-ninth election.

segments.speaker: Inna
segments.body: That's a difficult position for affected citizens. The ombudsman, Spain's rights watchdog, wants the appeal treated as exceptionally urgent. right What is happening at the consulates?

segments.speaker: Dima
segments.body: The Foreign Ministry says some consulates cannot compile all the necessary data before election day. That leaves the offices implementing the suspension under considerable time pressure.

segments.speaker: Inna
segments.body: In the election campaign, a Sigma Dos poll for El Mundo projects a combined two hundred and one seats for PP and Vox. Its most likely scenario gives a hundred and seventeen to PSOE, Frente Amplio and Podemos together. The survey was conducted in the first half of October.

segments.speaker: Dima
segments.body: Huh. That's a wide gap between those groups. It gives the parties very different starting points for the campaign.

segments.speaker: Inna
segments.body: And the campaign appeals are already quite direct.

segments.speaker: Dima
segments.body: PP leader and prime ministerial candidate Alberto Núñez Feijóo appealed to Catalonia yesterday for a large majority supporting a change of government. Europa Press reports that his call came ahead of the general election. He is seeking Catalan backing as part of his bid to become Prime Minister.

segments.speaker: Inna
segments.body: On the left, ERC lead candidate and congressional spokesman Gabriel Rufián has apologised for the failure to unite. In an interview broadcast on October seventeenth, he urged disillusioned supporters to vote, 20 Minutos reports. He said he wished Podemos and Frente Amplio had reached an agreement before the election.

segments.speaker: Dima
segments.body: Oof. He's asking disappointed supporters to vote while acknowledging why they're disappointed. That's a difficult message to deliver.

segments.speaker: Inna
segments.body: He didn't hold back, either. He called the attempt at a united left an absolute failure.

segments.speaker: Dima
segments.body: On housing, El Mundo reports that a decree would apply ten percent VAT to all tourist flats from December first. Published in the official state gazette, it awaits parliamentary confirmation. Owners could deduct VAT on costs such as cleaning and repairs, potentially limiting the shift towards long-term rentals.

segments.speaker: Inna
segments.body: Hold on, owners could deduct some costs too? Then the tax charged doesn't tell us the whole financial effect for someone running a tourist flat.

segments.speaker: Dima
segments.body: That's the catch. Depending on the city and the rental price, deductions could offset the VAT. So it may still pay to keep renting short-term, and the move into longer leases may be limited.

segments.speaker: Inna
segments.body: The wider supply shortage is stark. Spain completed about eighty-one thousand homes between July last year and June this year. Almost two hundred and thirty-nine thousand new households formed, 20 Minutos reports. Only Cáceres and Soria avoided a shortfall. The shortage is pushing up purchase and rental prices, especially in populated areas.

segments.speaker: Dima
segments.body: That's a big mismatch. Whether you're looking to rent or buy, more households are competing for a supply that isn't keeping pace.

segments.speaker: Inna
segments.body: Housing starts are up this year, but completed homes have barely moved.

segments.speaker: Dima
segments.body: In brief, El Mundo reports another delay to national statistics on inactive workers with permanent but intermittent jobs. Experts estimate eight hundred thousand to nine hundred thousand are inactive and excluded from unemployment figures. Wider use of these contracts since twenty twenty-one makes the missing data more significant.

segments.speaker: Inna
segments.body: And on working arrangements, a UGT union study says more than three million people already work remotely. More than three point four million others could work from home, but employers don't allow it, El Diario reports. The union blames a culture that puts office attendance first.

segments.speaker: Dima
segments.body: Really, almost as many people blocked from remote work as already doing it? That makes this about employer decisions, not just whether a job can be done at home.

segments.speaker: Inna
segments.body: UGT's José Varela says that if only half of them were allowed to telework, Spain would exceed the EU average. interesting

segments.speaker: Dima
segments.body: The priority today is the flood emergency: keep checking official alerts in the affected areas.
